cues.en: Today I have a short update for you regarding the best toaster ever produced.

cues.en: For those that are new around here, a little over a year ago I made a video

cues.en: and without any input from the user.

cues.en: If you haven’t seen that video and are interested in knowing what makes the bread go down and up

cues.en: or touch in the middle of the video somewhere on your phone and it’ll be there in the top right.

cues.zh: 就是想告诉大家这一点！
cues.en: Just thought I’d let y’all know that!

cues.zh: 至于用智能电视之类设备观看的朋友，
cues.en: For those of you watching on a smart TV or whatever,

cues.en: well I'm sorry, but I do put links in the description, too.

cues.zh: 总之，今天要讲的是恒温器。
cues.en: Anyway, today’s focus is on the thermostat.

cues.zh: 它确实是这台烤面包机的核心部件
cues.en: That is in fact the central feature of this toaster

cues.zh: （好吧，其实核心部件是加热元件……）
cues.en: (well, actually the central feature is the heating element core... )

cues.zh: 但我的意思是，
cues.en: but I mean

cues.zh: 它是最重要的部件，至少从名字来看是这样，
cues.en: most important feature, or at least seems to be given its name,

cues.zh: 因为它赋予了 Radiant Control 中的 “Control” 这一部分。
cues.en: as it puts the radiant and control into Radiant Control.

cues.zh: 和现代吐司机不同，这类吐司机的两侧各有两排发热元件，
cues.en: These toasters, unlike modern ones, have two columns of heating elements on the sides,

cues.zh: 这样温控器的双金属片就能放在
cues.en: and that allows for the thermostat’s bimetallic strip to sit

cues.zh: 它们中间，通过热辐射被面包表面加热。
cues.en: between them and be warmed by the bread’s surface through radiation.

cues.zh: 面包本身挡住了中央发热元件对它的直射，而这些小金属鳍片
cues.en: It is shielded from the central heating element by the bread itself and these little metal fins shield

cues.zh: 则挡住了来自侧面发热元件的热量。
cues.en: it from the side elements.

cues.zh: 这样一来，它主要就是被正在烘烤的面包加热的。
cues.en: That makes it such that it becomes warmed mostly by the bread being toasted.

cues.zh: 你可能会问：“为什么要这么做？”
cues.en: You might ask, “why do it that way?”

cues.zh: 按 Sunbeam 的说法，这能让吐司机每一次都能把吐司烤到极致完美。
cues.en: Well, according to Sunbeam, this allows the toaster to toast the toast to toasted perfection every toast.

cues.zh: 他们是对的！完全没说错。
cues.en: And they’re right! Gloriously right.

cues.zh: 让温控器直接对面包的表面温度做出反应，可以排除掉
cues.en: Having the thermostat react to the surface temperature of the bread allows it to eliminate

cues.zh: 各种变量，比如吐司机本身的温度、面包的具体特性，
cues.en: variables such as the temperature of the toaster itself, the particular properties of the bread,

cues.zh: 以及促使我制作这个视频的另一个变量
cues.en: or the other variable which moved me to make this video

cues.zh: ——面包本身的初始温度。
cues.en: - the temperature of the bread.

cues.zh: 这台烤面包机真是又好又讨喜又健康又完美又令人愉快
cues.en: This toaster is such a good and nice and wholesome and perfect and pleasant toaster

cues.zh: 它改变了我的早餐习惯。
cues.en: that it has changed my breakfast routine.

cues.zh: 我从来都不太爱吃吐司，
cues.en: I was never much of a toast person,

cues.zh: 事实上，我已经很多年没有规律地吃过吐司了，
cues.en: in fact it had been years since I had toast with any regularity,

cues.zh: 所以对我来说，这似乎只是我「小厨房电器太多™」目录里的又一个新成员。
cues.en: so to me this seemed like yet another addition to my Too Many Small Kitchen Appliances™ catalog.

cues.zh: 但仅仅是因为能以如此自动化的方式为我准备好吐司，带来的纯粹喜悦
cues.en: But through the sheer delight of having my toast be prepared for me in such an automatic fashion

cues.zh: 简直像超自然的一样，
cues.en: that it’s practically supernatural,

cues.zh: 吐司成了我的最爱！
cues.en: toast has become my jam!

cues.zh: 而果酱正是我涂在吐司上的！
cues.en: And jam’s what I put on toast!

cues.zh: 促使我为你做这次更新的原因是它处理冷冻面包的方式。
cues.en: And the thing that pushed me to make this update for you was how this handles frozen bread.

cues.zh: 你看，目前的情况要求我们减少购买杂货的频率，
cues.en: You see, current circumstances require less frequent shopping for groceries with

cues.zh: 每次出门购买更大的量。
cues.en: larger amounts purchased with each outing.

cues.zh: 面包现在成了我常备的东西，
cues.en: As bread has now become a thing I have regularly,

cues.zh: 但这有点麻烦，因为面包的保质期实在短。
cues.en: this is somewhat problematic as bread sadly sports somewhat short shelf life.

cues.zh: 要是没先干掉，你就得靠流星来对付霉菌了。
cues.en: If it doesn’t dry out first, you’ll need some shooting stars to deal with the mold.

cues.zh: 不过当然，你也可以选择冷冻面包！
cues.en: But of course one has the option of freezing bread!

cues.zh: 把东西放进冷冻室就能放很久，面包也一样。
cues.en: Put something in the freezer and it lasts a long time, including bread.

cues.zh: 但如果你处理过一整条冻面包，你就知道那挺糟心的。
cues.en: However, if you’ve ever dealt with a loaf of frozen bread, you’ll know that it kinda stinks.

cues.zh: 想解冻又很难不变得湿软。
cues.en: It’s hard to let it thaw without getting soggy.

cues.zh: 如果你的目标是烤它，那用普通烤面包机你就得
cues.en: And if your goal is to toast it, well with a conventional toaster you’re gonna

cues.zh: 把烘烤档位调高不少，才能应对它是冻的这件事。
cues.en: have to adjust your toasting setting upwards quite a bit to deal with the fact that it’s frozen.

cues.zh: 也许经过大量实验后你能调得刚刚好，
cues.en: Maybe after a ton of experimentation you’ll dial it in just right,

cues.zh: 但忘了调回去，下一片新鲜面包就得进烧伤病房了。
cues.en: but forget to set it back and your next fresh slice will end up in the burn ward.

cues.zh: 但 Sunbeam Radiant Control 烤面包机可不一样！
cues.en: But not with the Sunbeam Radiant Control toaster!

cues.zh: 看好了。
cues.en: Watch what happens.

cues.zh: 这是一片新鲜的蜂蜜小麦面包。
cues.en: This is a slice of fresh honey-wheat bread.

cues.zh: 我把它放进烤面包机，看看烤好要多久。
cues.en: I’ll put it in the toaster and we’ll see how long it takes to toast.

cues.zh: 请欣赏我这尴尬的凝视，我真不该这么干，但我还是干了
cues.en: enjoy this awkward stare which I totally should not have done yet I did

cues.zh: 就这么久！
cues.en: It’s this long!

cues.zh: 现在来看看面包烤得怎么样。
cues.en: And now let’s take a look at what the bread looks like.

cues.zh: 这是新鲜的那片面包。没冻过；焦度是这样的。
cues.en: This here is our fresh slice of bread. This was not frozen; this is the darkness.

cues.zh: 我把它放在盘子里，等会儿好对比。
cues.en: I will put it on a plate so we can compare later.

cues.zh: 现在我拿一片冷冻过的同款面包。
cues.en: Now I’ll grab a slice of the same bread that’s been frozen.

cues.zh: 看，这片挺冰的
cues.en: See, this is quite cold

cues.zh: [手指弹面包的声音] 而且挺硬。
cues.en: [sound of bread being flicked by finger] and pretty hard.

cues.zh: 我完全没动过烤面包机的焦度调节——和烤新鲜面包时一模一样。
cues.en: I have not touched the darkness control on the toaster at all - it’s exactly the same as it was for the fresh bread.

cues.zh: 现在我把冷冻面包放进槽里，等着。
cues.en: So now I’ll put the frozen bread in the slot, and wait.

cues.zh: 好了！
cues.en: It’s done!

cues.zh: 现在来看看这片面包。
cues.en: So now let’s take a look at the bread.

cues.zh: 你看！颜色几乎一模一样——
cues.en: Would you look at that! It’s pretty much the same exact darkness -

cues.zh: （笑着说）说真的，我几乎完全分辨不出来——
cues.en: [through laughter] in fact I can hardly tell the difference at all -

cues.zh: 和新鲜面包片有什么区别。
cues.en: as the fresh slice.

cues.zh: 冷冻的……
cues.en: Frozen…

cues.zh: 新鲜的！
cues.en: Fresh!

cues.zh: 真不错！
cues.en: Pretty neat!

cues.zh: 而且不只是颜色一样。
cues.en: And it’s not just the color.

cues.zh: 从冷冻状态迅速烤到焦黄，烤出来的面包让你很难相信它之前冻过。
cues.en: Going quickly from frozen to toasted produces toast that you’d be hard-pressed to know was ever frozen.

cues.zh: 这又让我多了一个爱上这台烤面包机的理由。
cues.en: This has given me yet another reason to love this toaster.

cues.zh: 它通过间接测量面包表面的温度，
cues.en: Its indirect measurement of the bread’s surface temperature means that

cues.zh: 每次都能烤出完美效果，即使面包之前冻过也一样。
cues.en: it produces perfect results every time, even if the bread was frozen.

cues.zh: 我再问问全世界的烤面包机制造商：
cues.en: I say again to toaster manufacturers of the world;

cues.zh: 你们为什么做出来的烤面包机都这么糟糕？
cues.en: why are you making such terrible toasters?

cues.zh: 偶尔大家喜欢在推特上艾特我，推荐一些烤面包机，比如
cues.en: Occasionally y’all like to tweet at me with certain toaster models out there like a

cues.zh: 某款同样采用无拉杆设计的 Kitchen Aid，或是某种做工极其过度设计的
cues.en: Kitchen Aid model with a similar lever-less design or some sort of elaborately over-engineered

cues.zh: 动辄几百美元的日本烤面包机，然而……
cues.en: Japanese toaster which cost hundreds of dollars, and yet…

cues.zh: 这种“古老”的设计却依然经久不衰。
cues.en: this *ancient* design endures.

cues.zh: 它就是这么好用。
cues.en: It just works.

cues.zh: 而且我真正看重的甚至不是自动升降面包的功能
cues.en: And it’s not even the automatic bread lifting that I really care about

cues.zh: （好吧我说谎了，那功能酷毙了，大概也是我最近又开始吃吐司的原因）
cues.en: (OK that’s a lie; it’s fascinating and probably why I’m eating toast again)

cues.zh: 真正让它脱颖而出的
cues.en: it’s the thermostat design

cues.zh: 是它的温控器设计。
cues.en: that really sets it apart.

cues.zh: 正如我们在第一期烤面包机视频中发现的那样
cues.en: As we discovered in the first toaster video

cues.zh: （就是讲烤面包机里的电磁铁那一期）
cues.en: (the one about the electromagnet in your toaster)

cues.zh: 厂商们采用基于时间的断电机制已经有年头了，
cues.en: manufacturers have been using time-based trips for a while,

cues.zh: 他们甚至聪明到在控制电路中
cues.en: and they’ve even been so clever as to design temperature-compensation

cues.zh: 加入了温度补偿，以应对刚刚使用过、机身尚热的情况。
cues.en: into the control circuitry to account for a just-used hot toaster.

cues.zh: 我确信这台烤面包机在成本优化上已经超乎想象，但它告诉我们
cues.en: I’m sure that has been Cost-Optimized Beyond Belief but this toaster shows us that

cues.zh: 一根简单的双金属片反而能做到客观上更好的效果（只要实现正确）。
cues.en: a simple bimetallic strip manages to do an objectively better job (if implemented correctly).

cues.zh: 它不仅能补偿烤面包机变热的情况，还能补偿面包是冷的。
cues.en: It not only compensates for a hot toaster, but for cold bread.

cues.zh: 不过，我们还有一些恼人的局限。
cues.en: Still, we have some pesky limitations.

cues.zh: 正如我在之前的视频里说的，这台烤面包机的面包导槽是固定的，
cues.en: As I said in the earlier video, this toaster has fixed bread guides

cues.zh: 对付贝果就不太行了。
cues.en: and wouldn’t be very happy with a bagel.

cues.zh: 当然，
cues.en: Now of course,

cues.zh: 你可以轻松地把烤面包机现代化，加上现代那种可挤压式的面包导槽，
cues.en: you could easily modernize the toaster to include the modern squeezy-type bread guide thingies,

cues.zh: 但特别是贝果可能仍然是个问题。
cues.en: but bagels in particular might still present a problem.

cues.zh: 如果贝果的孔正好对着双金属片的位置，
cues.en: If the hole lines up with where the bimetallic strip is,

cues.zh: 烤面包机就会像里面根本没放面包一样，过早跳闸。
cues.en: the toaster will trip very prematurely like it does when there’s no bread in it at all.

cues.zh: 但其实……这就是我能想到的唯一局限了。
cues.en: But actually… well that’s the only limitation I can think of.

cues.zh: 这台烤面包机告诉我们，用面包本身来判断烤好没有
cues.en: This toaster shows us that actually using the bread as a means to determine doneness

cues.zh: 远比单纯设个计时器要好得多。
cues.en: is wildly better than just setting a timer.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，不止是冷冻面包，用温度还能兼顾
cues.en: I mean, going beyond just frozen bread, using temperature also helps account

cues.zh: 更紧实的面包、更薄或更厚的切片，以及一大堆其他变量。
cues.en: for things like denser breads, thinner or thicker slices, and a whole slew of other variables.

cues.zh: 为什么我们非要把时间当作判断吐司烤没烤好的唯一标准？
cues.en: Why have we made time the be-all end-all determinant for toast doneness?

cues.zh: 我们明明有这技术！
cues.en: We have the technology!

cues.zh: 造更好的烤面包机啊！
cues.en: Make better toasters!

cues.zh: 那种手持激光测温仪似乎很适合做现代传感器。
cues.en: Those little hand-held laser thermometer things seem like a good candidate for a modern sensor.

cues.zh: 只要在加热元件所在的侧面开个窗口
cues.en: Just make a window through the sides where the heating elements are

cues.zh: 然后测量面包表面就行了！
cues.en: and measure the surface of the bread!

cues.zh: 这甚至会比 Sunbeam 那款更精确！
cues.en: I mean it would be even more precise than the Sunbeam!

cues.zh: 精确到 literally“一直烤到面包达到 237.8 度”之类的程度。
cues.en: It could literally be as precise as “toast until the bread reaches 237.8 degrees” or whatever.

cues.zh: 真的。
cues.en: Really.

cues.zh: 拜托。
cues.en: Come on.

cues.zh: 这样做或许能解决使用那些奇怪卷曲加热元件的问题
cues.en: Doing that could help solve the problem of using those wierd curly-Q heating elements

cues.zh: 在两侧。
cues.en: on the sides.

cues.zh: 肯定有足够小的传感器，可以直接通过一个孔窥探……
cues.en: Surely there are small enough sensors to just take a peek through a hole in…

cues.zh: 不管这是什么材料。
cues.en: whatever material this is.

cues.zh: 哦！这也能解决百吉饼中间孔的问题！
cues.en: Oh! And it could solve the hole-in-the bagel problem, too!

cues.zh: 只要放几个传感器，忽略那些立刻变得超热的就行。
cues.en: Just have a few sensors and ignore any that go super hot right away.

cues.zh: 说实话，如果未来五年内没人能造出一款价格合理、能在基本烤面包能力上胜过这台名副其实的古董的烤面包机，
cues.en: Honestly if nobody makes a reasonably-priced toaster in the next five years that can best this literal antique

cues.zh: 在基本烤面包能力方面，
cues.en: in terms of basic toast-making ability,

cues.en: well I’ll be so perturbed as to draft a letter!

cues.zh: 等一下。
cues.en: Wait a minute.

cues.en: I smell the potential to use the word "algorithmically."

cues.en: Probably in wildly over-engineered form.

cues.zh: 而且我敢打赌它们还很“智能”。

cues.en: And some snark!

cues.zh: 我只是最近才有理由把面包冷冻起来。
cues.en: I just hadn’t had a reason to freeze any bread until recently.

cues.zh: 我当时第一个念头是：“你知道吗，我敢打赌 Sunbeam 肯定能把这片面包烤得恰到好处。”
cues.en: My first thought was “you know, I bet the Sunbeam will just toast this perfectly”

cues.zh: 结果果然没让我失望！
cues.en: and I was not disappointed!

cues.zh: 真的。
cues.en: Seriously.

cues.zh: 所有做烤面包机的人。
cues.en: All of you making toasters.

cues.zh: 就研究研究这款吧。
cues.en: Just study this one.

cues.zh: 就算你们坚持用那种靠电磁铁吓你一跳、弹簧弹出的设计，我也不介意，只要……
cues.en: I won’t even mind if you stick to the electromagnet scares-your-socks-off spring-loaded design, just…

cues.zh: 把面包烤好就行，别把智能功能搞得太复杂。
cues.en: make it toast well without going overboard on the smartness.

cues.zh: Sunbeam在40年代就证明了，能测温的烤面包机有多棒。
cues.en: Sunbeam proved back in the ‘40s how great a temperature-sensing toaster is.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们在21世纪可以再做一款。
cues.en: I think we can make one again in the 21st century.

cues.zh: 加个合理的百吉饼模式，把面包导轨现代化，槽口稍微加宽一点，方便放那些
cues.en: Add a reasonable bagel mode, modernize the bread guides, widen the slots a bit for fancy

cues.zh: 花式面包，那就行了。
cues.en: loafs of bread, and you’re good.

cues.zh: 你只需要好好营销，就能一炮而红。
cues.en: You’ll just need to market it properly, and you’ll have a hit on your hands.

cues.zh: 这可是免费建议，各位。我甚至承诺，任何这样的烤面包机
cues.en: This is free advice, people. I even promise to test any-such toaster

cues.zh: 只要上市售价低于50美元，我就来测试并做个视频。
cues.en: that may make it to market for less than $50 and make a video about it.

cues.zh: 你们都不用寄给我，我自己买。
cues.en: You don’t even need to send me one. I’ll just buy it.

cues.zh: 真的，你们都该为这台烤面包机感到无地自容。
cues.en: Really, you all should be absolutely embarrassed by this toaster.

cues.zh: 快点快点！
cues.en: Now chop chop!

cues.zh: ♫ 创新流畅爵士乐 ♫
cues.en: ♫ innovatively smooth jazz ♫

cues.zh: 你可能会问……
cues.en: You might ask…

cues.zh: 开始提词器！
cues.en: start the teleprompter!

cues.zh: 哦糟了。
cues.en: Oh ssshoot.

cues.zh: 呃啊。
cues.en: UGGHH.
Stupid…

cues.zh: 还记得提词器那期视频里我说过“别用我用的那个软件”吗？
cues.en: remember in the teleprompter video when I said “don’t use the software I use?”

cues.zh: 这就是原因啊啊啊……
cues.en: This is whyyyyy….

cues.zh: 建议你先通过我提供的那个卡片看一遍。
cues.en: I’d suggest you watch it first through that car(d) I’ve provided.

cues.zh: 卡片。
cues.en: Card.

cues.zh: 我可没给你提供车！
cues.en: I did not provide you with a car!

cues.zh: 那个视频简单提到了我——
cues.en: That video touched briefly on what I’m a going abadehbuh

cues.zh: 只是想让你们……知道——
cues.en: Just thought I’d let yaknall… knoeughblblb

cues.zh: 我刚写完这些台词！怎么会忘？
cues.en: I just wrote these lines! How could I forget them?

cues.zh: 这视频我玩得太开心了……
cues.en: I’m having too much fun with this video…

cues.zh: 如果它没干透……啊，漏了个词！
cues.en: If it doesn’t dry out… ahh, missed a word!

cues.zh: 如果整行对齐到……上？和。什么？
cues.en: If the whole lines up to… up? With. What?

cues.zh: 如果洞对齐到……fff
cues.en: If the hole lines up to… fff

cues.zh: 我怎么又说“对齐到”了？
cues.en: why did I say up to again?

cues.zh: 和。
cues.en: Up with.

cues.zh: 好了。认识做烤面包机的人吗？
cues.en: Alright. Know anyone who makes toasters?

cues.zh: 你有责任让他们看这个视频，好让他们为自己的无能感到羞愧。
cues.en: It is your duty to get them to watch this video so they can be ashamed of their ineptitude.

cues.zh: 听起来很苛刻，但真的。
cues.en: It sounds harsh but really.

cues.zh: 这根本没有任何借口。
cues.en: There are just no excuses for this.

cues.zh: 一点都没有。
cues.en: None at all.
